en.headline: Air quality reaches serious levels, experts urge elderly to stay indoors
en.dek: The Environmental Protection Department recorded serious and very high health risk levels at several stations amid elevated ozone, with conditions expected to persist for a few more days.
body: Air quality health risk levels rose to serious and very high at several monitoring stations in recent days, prompting health advice for vulnerable groups.

The Environmental Protection Department’s Air Quality Health Index reached a serious level at the Tuen Mun station on Wednesday afternoon and remained elevated for consecutive hourly readings. On Thursday, stations including Central/Western, Southern, Tsuen Wan, Tuen Mun and Sha Tin recorded high levels, with the Southern station later reaching very high.

Experts attributed the surge mainly to elevated ozone levels driven by sunlight and high temperatures under relatively weak winds. They warned that the conditions were likely to continue over the next few days and advised the elderly, children and people with heart or respiratory conditions to reduce outdoor physical activity and stay indoors until later in the day when possible.
The public can check the latest hourly readings and forecasts on the Environmental Protection Department’s AQHI website.

zh.headline: 空氣質素達嚴重水平 專家建議長者留在室內
zh.dek: 環保署多個監測站錄得嚴重及甚高健康風險級別，主因臭氧水平上升，料情況未來數日持續。
body: 本港多個空氣質素監測站近日健康風險級別升至嚴重及甚高，當局及專家向易受影響人士發出健康建議。
環保署空氣質素健康指數周三下午在屯門站達嚴重水平，並持續數個小時。周四中西區、南區、荃灣、屯門及沙田等站錄得高水平，南區其後更達甚高水平。
專家指，主要原因是陽光充足及氣溫高企加上風勢偏弱，令臭氧水平上升。他們預期情況未來數日仍會持續，建議長者、兒童及有心臟病或呼吸系統疾病的人士減少戶外體力活動，並盡量在日間較後時間前留在室內。
市民可在環保署空氣質素健康指數網站查閱最新每小時讀數及預測。
